needs_human.note: A stat failure other than file-not-found is treated as 'file absent' and empties a sole owner's pointer; the spec only defines the absent case (F-6).; A scan-detected move of a row with an empty or dangling pointer defers generation to the next scan; I3 and I16 do not say which one wins (F-5).; With the old addon pin, the media_import startup caption retry writes .loft rows back to path form with a new mtime and ETag, so each later startup migrates them again. decisions.md records this; the spec's delivery note covers only 'migrates at the next startup', and does not mention the repeat or the ETag change.

A stat failure other than not-found during migration is treated as an absent file (thumbnail.py:707-710), and the spec does not define this case.; A non-regular file at a pointer's path is also treated as absent (thumbnail.py:711-712), and the spec does not state this.

A stat error other than not-found counts as an absent file during migration (MIG-1).; Two rows naming one absent path string form a shared group and are both emptied, even if each has a slot file, whereas I10's wording repoints a row with an existing slot. I found no ordinary way to reach this: a shared group commits its emptied pointers before unlinking, so a stopped run cannot produce it. An existing slot would be stranded, and a .loft would lose its picture.; A scan-detected move of a row with an empty or dangling .by-id pointer no longer generates in that scan, because _relocate_thumbnail is gone. The placeholder stays until the next scan. This agrees with I3 and I16, but the spec does not state the one-scan delay.
